newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Wills says improves market share.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Wills says improves market share.

text.p: Cigarette maker W.D. & H.O. Wills Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday it had increased both market share and sales volume in calendar 1996.
Wills said its ex-factory sales rose 3.1 percent in 1996, despite a contraction in the total Australian market for manufactured cigarettes.
Its shipment market share, which measures product sold to wholesalers and retailers, rose 1.3 percent to 28.6 percent at year end, the company said in a statement
Wills earlier reported a net profit for 1996 of A$13.27 million, against a A$5.16 million loss in 1995 following a cigarette price-war.
The result included an abnormal loss of $9.7 million relating to redundancy costs and a strategic review of operations.

Legal costs relating to a product liability claim, filed against the three Australian tobacco manufacturers last year and expected to go to trial this year, added another A$9.5 million to abnormals, it said.
Wills, which is about 67 percent owned by B.A.T. Industries Plc, also wrote back a A$4.1 million contingency provision as an abnormal profit following the successful outcome of a tax case.
Chief executive Stuart Watterton said a sharp fall in price discounting and improved cost control added to the result.

The company's premium brand Benson & Hedges increased market share despite severing its ties with Australian cricket due to Federal government legislation, he said. Horizon, its biggest selling brand, also boosted market share.
